name: Na Du
title: Assistant Professor
department: Department of Informatics and Networked Systems, School of Computing and Information
researchAreas: Gaze-aware target grounding and intent understanding
fitReason: Strong software-oriented HRI fit: multimodal intent recognition, gaze/language grounding, user-aware explanations and learned visual scene reasoning. A bounded data/model-evaluation or nonclinical interface project is a more plausible eight-week scope than initiating a new patient study.

physicalEvidence.summary: A primary author report for the coauthored HRI 2025 study documents a prototype combining a robotic arm, camera and Unity-based simulated interface, used to explain the system during interviews with 13 powered-wheelchair users. This is collaborative physical-prototype evidence, not proof of autonomous language-to-action execution, a wholly physical interface, or Na Du's exclusive robot inventory. A separate coauthored ICORR 2025 abstract describes users manually controlling a robot arm in a kitchen task with light/sound feedback; full methods and exact arm model were not accessible in this pass.

shortVisit.summary: Her live prospective-student page explicitly says she may host visiting undergraduate or graduate students and scholars depending on research interests and funding. It provides a dedicated visitor inquiry subject and requests CV, transcript, research background and optional writing/publication samples. No duration, summer 2027 slot or lab funding promise is stated. Existing Pitt international-visitor policy notes provide a conditional administrative route after host acceptance, not a lab offer.

scoreReasons.fit: direct multimodal HRI/grounding plus current learned perception, though not primarily robot-policy learning.
scoreReasons.physical: attributable collaborative arm prototypes/manual control; exact hardware and independent lab access remain unverified.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: explicit graduate-inclusive visitor inquiry, conditional on fit/funding and with unspecified duration.
scoreReasons.freshness: September 2026 primary paper and dated university seminar. This is provisional fit/evidence scoring, not acceptance probability or prestige.

unknowns: The distinct undergraduate/master's research-assistantship paragraph is limited to Pitt students and requires a prior semester of project work; it must not be substituted for the separate visiting-student invitation.

International appointment, degree-related training, funding documentation, permitted activities and exact visit length require host and Pitt OIS approval. Self-funded willingness alone does not establish an approved appointment.

Pitt's J-1 Student Intern route has activity restrictions including clinical patient care/contact and elder-care settings; a proposed assistive-robot project must be classified by OIS rather than presumed eligible.
The September 2026 computer-vision paper evaluates existing driving-video datasets. It is AI-method evidence, not physical-car deployment evidence.
The 2026 domestic-robot goal-alignment study is a survey, and the multimodal instruction work should not be counted as hardware autonomy without its methods.
Public robot research does not confirm current equipment access, a summer 2027 offer or host availability.
